title.en: World Desk
title.zh: 全球焦点

strap.en: A fast view of global affairs, conflict, diplomacy, and human need.
strap.zh: 快速掌握国际局势、冲突、外交与人类处境。

title.en: News live: dozens of Australians believed to be among hundreds missing in Nepal flash floods
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪灾致数百人失踪，包括数十名澳大利亚人

summary.en: Dozens of Australians are believed to be among hundreds of people missing following powerful flash floods in Nepal that swept away homes, roads, and bridges. Australian officials are preparing to offer consular assistance to their citizens affected by the disaster.
summary.zh: 尼泊尔发生强力洪水，冲毁房屋、道路和桥梁，导致数百人失踪，其中包括数十名澳大利亚人。澳大利亚官员正准备为受灾公民提供领事援助。

body.en: Powerful floods in Himalayan border area sweep away houses, roads and bridges. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The prime minister, Anthony Albanese , says Dfat officials are ready to provide consular assistance to Australians in Nepal, after the devastating flooding in the country. A local tourism official said they believed 34 Australians were missing in the area, among hundreds of foreign nationals. Australian officials were not confirming numbers at this stage, and were working to check on the welfare of people they know were in the affected region. Australians in the affected area should follow the advice of local authorities. We are aware of a number of Australians in the area and Australian officials are urgently working to confirm their welfare. We are liaising with local authorities as well as tour operators. We stand ready to provide consular assistance. The images are very disturbing indeed. We do know that there are Australians in the area. We don’t know exactly how many. Continue reading...
body.zh: 喜马拉雅边境地区的强大洪水冲毁了房屋、道路和桥梁。关注今天的新闻直播 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞 (Anthony Albanese) 表示，在尼泊尔遭受毁灭性洪灾之后，外交部官员已准备好向在尼泊尔的澳大利亚人提供领事援助。当地旅游官员表示，他们相信该地区有 34 名澳大利亚人失踪，其中包括数百名外国人。澳大利亚官员现阶段尚未确认具体数字，并正在努力检查他们所知道的受影响地区民众的福利状况。受影响地区的澳大利亚人应遵循当地政府的建议。我们知道该地区有许多澳大利亚人，澳大利亚官员正在紧急努力确认他们的福利。我们正在与地方当局以及旅行社联络。我们随时准备提供领事协助。这些图像确实非常令人不安。我们确实知道该地区有澳大利亚人。我们不知道到底有多少。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the face of devastating floods in Nepal, the plight of hundreds missing, including many foreign nationals, calls for our attention and compassion. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves and to defend the rights of the poor and vulnerable, a principle that extends to supporting those caught in international crises.
reflection.zh: 在尼泊尔发生毁灭性洪水之际，数百人失踪，其中包括许多外国国民，他们的困境呼唤我们的关注和同情。《箴言》31:8-9提醒我们，要为不能为自己说话的人说话，为穷乏人和一切困苦的辩屈，这一原则也适用于支持那些身处国际危机中的人们。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Democratic states sue to block postal service from carrying out Trump’s mail-in voting order – US politics live
title.zh: 达琳·格雷厄姆赢得南卡罗来纳州共和党提名，接替她已故的兄弟进入美国参议院——美国政治直播

summary.en: Darline Graham, sister of the late Lindsey Graham, secured the Republican nomination for the US Senate in South Carolina, overcoming concerns about her lack of experience. She will now appear on the November ballot, having received backing from former President Trump.
summary.zh: 达琳·格雷厄姆，已故林赛·格雷厄姆的妹妹，赢得了南卡罗来纳州共和党美国参议院的提名，尽管有人担忧她缺乏经验。她获得了前总统特朗普的支持，现在将出现在11月的选票上。

body.en: Two dozen states file lawsuit days after supreme court lifts one injunction blocking part of president’s order Sign up for the US Breaking News email A US military strike on an alleged drug trafficking boat in the Caribbean on Tuesday killed four people, officials said. US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said in a post on X that the strike targeted a vessel “operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 得到特朗普支持的已故妹妹林赛·格雷厄姆 (Lindsey Graham) 克服了对在 11 月选举中缺乏经验的担忧 达林·格雷厄姆 (Darline Graham) 赢得美国参议院共和党初选 官员称，美国周二对加勒比海一艘涉嫌贩毒的船只发动军事袭击，造成四人死亡。美国南方司令部 (SOUTHCOM) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，这次袭击的目标是一艘“沿着加勒比地区既定的毒品贩运路线运行”的船只。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As Darline Graham prepares to potentially serve in the US Senate, the concerns raised about her lack of experience remind us that wisdom is essential for effective leadership. Whether in public office or daily life, we can seek Yahweh's guidance, knowing He gives generously to all who ask. This principle applies to any leader stepping into a significant...
reflection.zh: 随着达琳·格雷厄姆准备可能在美国参议院任职，人们对她缺乏经验的担忧提醒我们，智慧对于有效的领导至关重要。无论是在公职还是日常生活中，我们都可以寻求雅伟的指引，知道祂会慷慨地赐予所有祈求的人。这一原则适用于任何担任重要职务的领导者，他们将面临需要超越以往经验的复杂决策。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Man in prison in New York advances in primary for Alaska’s US House seat
title.zh: 纽约监狱中的男子在美国众议院阿拉斯加席位初选中获胜

summary.en: A man serving time in a federal prison in New York has advanced in the primary for Alaska's sole US House seat. Eric Hafner, a registered Democrat who is scheduled for release in 2036, also ran for the seat in 2024 and secured a spot on the general election ballot.
summary.zh: 一名正在纽约联邦监狱服刑的男子在阿拉斯加唯一一个美国众议院席位的初选中获胜。埃里克·哈夫纳是一名注册民主党人，定于2036年获释，他也参加了2024年的席位竞选，并获得了大选的投票资格。

body.en: Democrat Eric Hafner, to be released in 2036, also ran for seat in 2024, securing spot on that general election ballot A man who is serving time in a federal prison in New York advanced on Wednesday from the primary for Alaska’s lone US House seat. Eric Hafner, a registered Democrat, also ran for the seat in 2024 and secured a spot on the general election ballot that November despite a challenge brought by the Alaska Democratic party. Continue reading...
body.zh: 将于 2036 年出狱的民主党人埃里克·哈夫纳 (Eric Hafner) 也参加了 2024 年的席位竞选，确保了大选选票的席位。周三，一名在纽约联邦监狱服刑的男子从阿拉斯加唯一的美国众议院席位的初选中晋级。注册民主党人埃里克·哈夫纳 (Eric Hafner) 也在 2024 年竞选该席位，并在 11 月的大选选票中获得一席之地，尽管阿拉斯加州民主党提出了挑战。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of Eric Hafner, an incarcerated individual, advancing in a political primary challenges our assumptions about who can participate in civic life. Matthew 25:40 reminds us that whatever we do for the least among us, we do for Christ. This story invites reflection on how we view and engage with those who are marginalized or imprisoned, recognizing...
reflection.zh: 埃里克·哈夫纳（Eric Hafner）一名在押人员，却在美国众议院阿拉斯加席位初选中取得进展，这一消息挑战了我们对公民参与者身份的固有看法。《马太福音》25:40提醒我们，我们为最小的弟兄所做的，就是为基督所做的。这个故事促使我们反思如何看待和对待那些被边缘化或被监禁的人，认识到他们固有的尊严和潜力。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez rejoins DSA after membership lapse of seven years
title.zh: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯在七年后重新加入民主社会主义者组织

summary.en: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a prominent figure in American democratic socialism, has rejoined the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) after a seven-year hiatus. She initially joined the organization in 2018 as a House candidate but did not renew her membership after the first year. Her rejoining comes amid...
summary.zh: 美国民主社会主义的知名人物亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯（Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez）在中断七年后重新加入了美国民主社会主义者组织（DSA）。她最初于2018年作为众议院候选人加入该组织，但在一年后未续订会员资格。她重新加入之际，正值外界猜测她可能在2028年竞选总统。

body.en: Then House candidate joined Democratic Socialists of America in 2018 but didn’t renew membership after a year Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has rejoined the Democratic Socialists of America after not renewing her membership for seven years, amid speculation that she might run for president in 2028. The 36-year-old New York representative and one of the country’s most prominent democratic socialists renewed her membership in the group’s national organization after reports emerged earlier this month that it had lapsed. Ocasio-Cortez initially joined the group in 2018. Continue reading...
body.zh: 当时的众议院候选人于 2018 年加入美国民主社会主义者，但一年后没有续会。 亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯 (Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez) 在七年没有续会后，重新加入了美国民主社会主义者 (Democratic Socialists of America)，外界猜测她可能会在 2028 年竞选总统。这位 36 岁的纽约众议员、美国最著名的民主社会主义者之一，在本月早些时候有报道称该组织的全国组织已失效后，她续签了该组织的会员资格。 Ocasio-Cortez 最初于 2018 年加入该组织。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political affiliations can be complex, often intertwined with personal identity and ambition. The Apostle Paul urges believers to "do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves." As figures like Ocasio-Cortez navigate their political paths, may they be guided by a spirit of genuine service rather...
reflection.zh: 政治归属可能很复杂，常常与个人身份和野心交织在一起。使徒保罗敦促信徒“凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。” 随着像奥卡西奥-科尔特斯这样的政治人物在他们的政治道路上导航，愿他们以真正的服务精神为指导，而非自私自利，寻求共同的福祉而非个人利益。

verse.textEn: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.
verse.textZh: 凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。

title.en: US drug agency approves breakthrough treatment for pancreatic cancer
title.zh: 美国药监局批准胰腺癌突破性疗法

summary.en: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved daraxonrasib, a new drug for pancreatic cancer that nearly doubled survival times in clinical trials compared to standard chemotherapy. Experts describe the daily pill as a game changer for one of the world's deadliest and most difficult-to-treat diseases.
summary.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准了名为 daraxonrasib 的胰腺癌新药。临床试验显示，与标准化学疗法相比，该药使患者的生存时间从6.6个月延长至13.2个月，几乎翻了一番。专家称这种每日服用的药物是治疗这种全球最致命且最难治愈癌症之一的“游戏规则改变者”。

body.en:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved a treatment for pancreatic cancer that, in clinical trials, nearly doubled the overall survival time for patients.

The drug, daraxonrasib, sold under the brand name Rasonque and manufactured by Revolution Medicines, appears to be a breakthrough in treating one of the world's deadliest cancers.

A late-stage clinical trial with 500 patients found those who took the daily pill had an average survival time of 13.2 months, compared to 6.6 months for those on chemotherapy.

The FDA said the drug provided a "critical new option for patients facing an extraordinarily difficult and historically hard-to-treat cancer".

Daraxonrasib helps prevent the spread of cancer by locking onto and shutting off the mutated KRAS gene, which is in more than 90% of pancreatic tumours and spurs cancer growth.

Each year, roughly 67,000 people in the US are diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, which has the highest mortality rate of all major cancers, according to the American Cancer Society..

Pancreatic cancer is often spotted late and is notoriously difficult to treat. More than half of those with pancreatic cancer die within three months of diagnosis.

In 2025, the FDA granted the drug a "Breakthrough Therapy" designation, given to treatments for serious conditions that warrant an expedited review.

The agency then approved the drug six months ahead of the regulatory deadline because it "showed unprecedented results in an area of high unmet need", said Angelo de Claro, director of the the agency's Oncology Center of Excellence.

The most common side effects of the treatment were rash, diarrhoea, nausea, fatigue and vomiting, the FDA said. About 44% of patients on daraxonrasib experienced severe side effects, compared to 57.5% treated with chemotherapy in the trial.

Former US Senator Ben Sasse, who announced in December he had been diagnosed with Stage 4 pancreatic cancer, is in a clinical trial for the drug and has said it has helped shrink his tumours.
body.zh: 美国食品和药物管理局已批准一种治疗胰腺癌的疗法，在临床试验中，该疗法使患者的总生存时间几乎延长了一倍。 这种名为 daraxonrasib 的药物以 Rasonque 为品牌销售，由 Revolution Medicines 生产，似乎是治疗世界上最致命的癌症之一的突破。 一项对 500 名患者进行的后期临床试验发现，每天服用药物的患者平均生存时间为 13.2 个月，而接受化疗的患者平均生存时间为 6.6 个月。 FDA 表示，该药物“为面临极其困难且历史上难以治疗的癌症的患者提供了一个重要的新选择”。 Daraxonrasib 通过锁定和关闭突变的 KRAS 基因来帮助防止癌症扩散，该基因存在于 90% 以上的胰腺肿瘤中，并会刺激癌症生长。 根据美国癌症协会的数据，美国每年约有 67,000 人被诊断患有胰腺癌，这是所有主要癌症中死亡率最高的癌症。 胰腺癌通常发现较晚，而且治疗起来非常困难。超过一半的胰腺癌患者在诊断后三个月内死亡。 2025 年，FDA 授予该药物“突破性疗法”称号，用于治疗需要快速审查的严重疾病。 该机构肿瘤学卓越中心主任 Angelo de Claro 表示，该机构比监管截止日期提前六个月批准了该药物，因为它“在高度未满足的需求领域显示出前所未有的成果”。 FDA 表示，治疗最常见的副作用是皮疹、腹泻、恶心、疲劳和呕吐。大约 44% 的 daraxonrasib 患者出现严重副作用，而试验中接受化疗的患者这一比例为 57.5%。 美国前参议员 Ben Sasse 在 12 月宣布自己被诊断出患有第四期胰腺癌，目前正在对该药物进行临床试验，并表示该药物有助于缩小他的肿瘤。

reflection.en: The discovery that daraxonrasib can extend the lives of those facing pancreatic cancer is a profound testament to the value of persistent scientific inquiry. By searching out the biological mechanisms of this deadly disease, researchers have turned a historically hard-to-treat diagnosis into a moment of tangible hope. We recognize the dignity of this work,...
reflection.zh: 发现 daraxonrasib 能够延长胰腺癌患者的生命，有力地证明了坚持科学探究的价值。通过探寻这种致命疾病的生物学机制，研究人员将“历史上难以治疗”的诊断转变为切实的希望。我们认可这项工作的尊严，它通过拒绝让生命中最艰难的谜团永远尘封，表达了对雅伟所赐予的生命之礼的尊重。

verse.textEn: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter; to search out a matter is the glory of kings.
verse.textZh: 将事隐秘乃神的荣耀；将事察清乃君王的荣耀。

title.en: A landmark US deal could change social media forever
title.zh: 美国达成里程碑式协议，或将永远改变社交媒体

summary.en: Meta Platforms has agreed to pay up to $25 billion over the next decade to settle lawsuits from nearly all 50 US states alleging that Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict children. The deal includes strict new limits on how teenagers interact with these platforms to address concerns over mental health and...
summary.zh: Meta公司已同意在未来十年内支付高达250亿美元，以解决美国近50个州发起的诉讼。这些州指控Facebook和Instagram的设计旨在让儿童成瘾。该协议还包括对青少年使用这些平台的严格新限制，以应对对其心理健康和安全的担忧。

body.en:
Meta Platforms will pay up to US$18 billion ($25 billion) over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram under an agreement with nearly all 50 US states that took it to trial to resolve claims it designed those social media platforms to addict children.

The settlements announced on Wednesday end a federal trial over allegations Meta's products harmed children, and the company misled the public about their safety. Four of the states — California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey — were expected to seek close to US$200 billion ($279 billion) in civil penalties.

While Meta will not undergo a fundamental overhaul, the accords represent a sweeping effort to define how it serves young users.

It could provide a template for resolving thousands of other lawsuits against social media companies. Governments around the world are trying to curb children's access to harmful online content, including a ban in Australia on social media for children under 16.

“The focus of this case was to protect our kids," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said in a statement. "The relief we are getting in this settlement is very meaningful and well beyond what any court has ordered or is likely to order."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Meta agreed over the next decade to restrict teenagers' use of Facebook and Instagram to two hours a day and block all usage from midnight to 6am, absent parental consent.

These limits could be tightened if the social media platforms Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube adopt similar terms. Meta will also disable most push notifications to teenage users during school hours of 8am to 3pm and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content.

The settlement does not require Meta to abandon personalised recommendations or targeted advertising. It also does not address some content Meta researchers found particularly problematic, including posts that made Instagram users uncomfortable with their body image.

Meta denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle. The total payout represents about three to four months of profit and about one month of revenue for Meta.

"Ensuring teens have a safe and productive experience on our platforms is an absolute imperative for Meta," the Menlo Park, California-based company said in a blog post. "We want to get this right for parents and teens."

Meta agreed to make maximum payments of about US$16.7 billion ($22 billion) to 47 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands.

title.en: Australians among hundreds missing after floods and landslides in Nepal
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
A massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 160 people on Wednesday and left several hundred missing, including a reported 34 Australians.

Aid workers said entire settlements had been "wiped out". Surveillance footage verified by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency shows dozens of people running for their lives as a stories-tall surge of debris slammed into the Chinese side of a border area, tossing lorries and buses aside.

Chinese state media reported "major casualties" from a mudslide at a Tibet border hub, reporting three dead and another 265 people missing.

Nepali police said that they had recovered 157 bodies after "devastating floods", with officers "working to move families in flood-risk areas ... to safer locations."

Rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Some 403 tourists — 341 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for several hours after the disaster struck, according to Nepal's tourism ministry.

A list provided to ABC News by tourism board spokesman puts the number of missing Australians at 34.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) is yet to confirm that number.

"We are aware of a number of Australians in the area and Australian officials are urgently working to confirm their welfare," a DFAT spokesperson told SBS News. "We are liaising with local authorities as well as tour operators."

The missing foreigners included 142 Indians, and others from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea and the United States, the tourism board said.

"Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out," said David Fisher, the Nepal head of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).

It said it was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags.

"The pain and loss you have suffered is not small," he said in a statement on social media. "But I want to assure you that you are not alone in this difficult time — the state is with you with all its means and resources."

Locals were traumatised, while experts cautioned that a lingering blockage in a river could produce an additional flood.

"I got a call from (my brother-in-law) this morning, and they were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing," said 56-year-old local Raju Bhadel.

But Nepal's Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said an earthquake likely triggered a landslide, which in turn blocked a...

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪、整个定居点“被夷为平地”的消息，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此大规模的毁灭和生命损失面前，“雅伟哭了”这简短的经文提醒我们，悲伤是一种自然而神圣的回应。雅伟在基督里分担我们人类的痛苦，当言语无法表达时，祂提供了一个充满怜悯的同在。

title.en: Rocky Horror Picture Show star Tim Curry dead at 80
title.zh: 《洛奇恐怖秀》主演蒂姆·克里去世，享年80岁

summary.en: Tim Curry, the English actor famous for his role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at 80 after struggling with his health for over a decade following a 2012 stroke.
summary.zh: 英国演员蒂姆·克里因在邪典音乐电影《洛奇恐怖秀》中饰演弗兰克-N-弗特博士而闻名，他在2012年中风后与病魔抗争十余载，现已去世，享年80岁。

body.en:
Tim Curry, the English actor best known for his star turn as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the cult classic musical film The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at the age of 80, US media reported Thursday.

Curry, who had struggled with his health for more than a decade after a debilitating stroke, died at his home in Los Angeles, TMZ said, citing unnamed sources.

The actor, who launched his career in London's West End theatre district, first played the gender-bending mad scientist in Rocky Horror before reprising the role in the 1975 film, which is still a staple of midnight cinema showings more than 50 years later.

His other credits include the sinister clown Pennywise in a 1990 television miniseries version of Stephen King's It and films that included Charlie's Angels and Muppet Treasure Island.

An impressive theatrical resume that began in the 1960s saw him do turns at the Royal Court Theatre and the Citizens Theatre, taking on roles written by Shakespeare, Brecht and Tom Stoppard, among others.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Curry was nominated for Tony and Olivier awards for his theatre work in New York and London.

One of his more memorable performances was on Broadway and in the West End as King Arthur in Monty Python's Spamalot, the stage adaptation of Monty Python and the Holy Grail.

His slightly cartoonish good looks and an unparalleled ability both to camp and to vamp meant he was much in demand for roles that required a certain air of villainy.

That was on display in Annie in 1982, when, as con artist Rooster Hannigan, he plots to kidnap the orphan girl.

Three years later, in Clue, he was the butler who corralled a country house full of murder suspects in the cinematic version of the board game.

There were straighter roles, including opposite Sean Connery in The Hunt for Red October, but his comedic talents shone brightest, even in small parts, like the Plaza Hotel concierge in Home Alone 2.

But it was Dr Frank-N-Furter, the "sweet transvestite from Transsexual, Transylvania," that defined his career.

Richard O'Brien's madcap stage creation tells the story of an unsuspecting young couple whose flat tire leads them into the house of a scientist who is creating a cross-dressing sexual plaything.

Along the way, there's a lot of singing, dancing and heavy dose of rocker Meatloaf.

The film, which flopped on its initial release, found life as a cult classic on the midnight showings circuit, with aficionados dressing up to sing and dance in the aisles and throw popcorn — and frankfurters — at the screen.

"It seemed like something that would go," Curry told a TV interviewer in 1970s London.

"I was hesitant in that, if it...

Yet, even as our physical selves may waste away, the Scripture offers hope that our inner spirit can be renewed day by day. This perspective encourages us to find strength and purpose beyond outward...

title.en: Australia is being urged to join a $41 trillion fight playing out in its backyard
title.zh: 澳大利亚被敦促加入一场在其后院上演的价值 41 万亿美元的战斗

summary.en: They're potato-sized, look like black truffles and sit at the centre of a growing South Pacific tussle.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Sitting at the bottom of the Pacific Ocean are vast deposits of the critical minerals that could drive a potential green transition.

The race to start mining these deposits has begun, and experts say what happens next could impact Australia's relationship with once-reliable Pacific allies.

Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific has been on the cards for many years, but the not-yet-existent industry had been on pause while a United Nations agency responsible for the ocean floor develops guidelines for extraction.

That changed last year when United States President Donald Trump's administration took the controversial step of issuing an executive order allowing US companies to apply for licences in its Pacific territories, sidestepping international law.

One US company has publicly committed to start operations as soon as 2027, and in August the US shocked Pacific island communities by announcing it planned to auction off a maritime territory near American Samoa for deep-sea mining.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In 2025, China signed a deal with the Cook Islands to co-operate on seabed mineral development and research and is reportedly considering a similar partnership with Kiribati.

Now the US and China are locked in a geopolitical battle in the Pacific to corner the industry — valued at up to US$30 trillion ($41.88 trillion) — before it's even begun.

The subject has starkly divided Pacific nations. Some want to cash in on the new mining boom, while others worry the largely untested industry could wreak havoc on the environment.

Experts warn this division could leave the region vulnerable to exploitation and damage Australia's relations with its closest regional partners.

Deep-sea mining as an industry does not yet exist, but the technology behind it does, and countries have been surveying the ocean floor for years to understand what kinds of deposits lie at the bottom of the ocean.

These deposits come in several forms, but extracting so-called 'polymetallic nodules' forms the backbone of existing deep-sea mining technology.

Formed layer by layer, over millions of years, these potato-sized forms are found between 3,500 and 6,500 metres beneath the surface.

To extract these deposits, a large harvesting vehicle drives across the pitch-black ocean floor, vacuuming up the deposits and the surface layer of sediment before pumping the material to the surface via a pipe for sorting.

The Lowy Institute's Connor Graham told SBS News Australia has two key reasons to be concerned about deep-sea mining in the Pacific.

title.en: Parrot eggs hatch after suspected Thai smuggler arrested at South African airport
title.zh: 泰国走私嫌疑人在南非机场被捕后鹦鹉蛋孵化

summary.en: A 50-year-old Thai suspect was arrested with the eggs in a "homemade incubator" carried as hand luggage.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Fifty eggs suspected to be those of endangered parrots were intercepted at South Africa's main airport in Johannesburg last Thursday - and some of them have now hatched.

A 50-year-old Thai national was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle them in a "homemade incubator bag" carried as hand luggage, according to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE).

Many of the rescued eggs have successfully hatched, with the chicks now receiving "intensive" care to "maximise their chances of survival", it added.

If convicted, the suspected wildlife trafficker faces a fine of up to 10m rand ($626,000, £461,000) or up to 10 years in prison, or both.

Initial investigations suggest the eggs belong to a parrot species protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (Cites).

The arrest followed a joint operation by the DFFE, the Green Scorpions - a specialised environmental enforcement unit - and various divisions of the police.

Environment Minister David Maynier has congratulated all the agencies involved, saying "illegal wildlife trafficking can only be challenged by a co-ordinated defence of our natural heritage".

He particularly thanked the dedicated staff at the National Zoological Garden in the capital, Pretoria, "who have been working tirelessly to incubate the seized eggs and provide specialised care to the hatchlings".

Last Thursday's arrest follows that of a 23-year-old Thai citizen in July, also caught at Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport, who was attempting to smuggle 418 parrot eggs.

The arrests highlighted the growing sophistication of transnational wildlife trafficking networks and reinforced "the importance of co-ordinated, intelligence-led law enforcement efforts", the DFFE said.

The illegal collection and trafficking of parrot eggs posed "a serious threat to wild bird populations and animal welfare", it added.

Officials explained that such eggs were often smuggled in improvised incubators and in conditions that endangered the welfare of developing embryos and hatchlings.

Wildlife trafficking remains a major threat in South Africa, one of the world's most biodiverse countries, with criminal networks frequently targeting animals such as elephants and pangolins, for sale on the international black market.

To combat the threat, the country adopted a new strategy six years ago to strengthen collaboration between government institutions, law enforcement agencies, conservation authorities, customs officials, prosecutors and international partners to dismantle criminal networks involved in the illicit wildlife trade.
body.zh: 上周四，南非约翰内斯堡主要机场截获了 50 个疑似濒临灭绝的鹦鹉蛋，其中一些现已孵化。 据林业、渔业和环境部 (DFFE) 称，一名 50 岁的泰国公民因涉嫌试图将其放入作为手提行李携带的“自制保温袋”中走私而被捕。 报告补充说，许多获救的鸡蛋已经成功孵化，小鸡现在正在接受“重症”护理，以“最大限度地提高生存机会”。 如果罪名成立，野生动物走私嫌疑人将面临最高 1000 万兰特（626,000 美元，461,000 英镑）的罚款或最高 10 年监禁，或两者并罚。 初步调查显示，这些蛋属于受《濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约》（Cites）保护的鹦鹉物种。 这次逮捕行动是由 DFFE、专门环境执法单位“绿蝎子队”和警察各部门联合采取的行动。 环境部长大卫·梅尼尔向所有相关机构表示祝贺，并表示“只有协调一致地保护我们的自然遗产，才能应对非法野生动物贩运”。 他特别感谢首都比勒陀利亚国家动物园的敬业工作人员，“他们一直在不知疲倦地孵化被查获的蛋，并为刚孵化的幼龟提供专门的照顾”。 上周四，一名 23 岁的泰国公民于 7 月在约翰内斯堡奥利弗·雷金纳德·坦博国际机场被捕，当时他正试图走私 418 个鹦鹉蛋。 DFFE 表示，此次逮捕行动凸显了跨国野生动物贩运网络日益复杂，并强化了“协调一致、情报主导的执法工作的重要性”。 报告补充说，非法收集和贩运鹦鹉蛋“对野生鸟类种群和动物福利构成严重威胁”。 官员们解释说，这些鸡蛋通常是在临时孵化器中走私的，其环境危及正在发育的胚胎和幼体的福利。 野生动物贩运仍然是南非这个世界上生物多样性最丰富的国家之一的主要威胁，犯罪网络经常以大象和穿山甲等动物为目标，在国际黑市上出售。 为了应对这一威胁，该国六年前采取了一项新战略，加强政府机构、执法机构、保护机构、海关官员、检察官和国际合作伙伴之间的合作，以瓦解参与非法野生动物贸易的犯罪网络。

title.en: Two German airport workers die of malaria after 'mosquito arrives on plane'
title.zh: “飞机上有蚊子”，两名德国机场工作人员死于疟疾

summary.en: It is believed the mosquitoes arrived at Germany's busiest airport on a plane, according to German public health officials.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two Frankfurt Airport workers have died of malaria after a rare outbreak led to six employees contracting the serious infection spread by mosquitoes.

It is believed the mosquitoes arrived at Germany's busiest airport on a plane, according to German public health officials, triggering an outbreak which was first detected in July.

A spokesperson for airport operator Fraport told the BBC an employee had died as a result of the infection, while public health officials said later on Wednesday that two of the affected individuals had died.

Traps have been installed at the airport and mosquitoes captured will be analysed in a laboratory to determine their species and origin.

"We have provided comprehensive information to all employees and encourage them to consult a doctor if they experience any symptoms," the Fraport spokesperson told the BBC.

The BBC understands that six male airport workers in different jobs and different areas of the airport were infected, and officials are analysing blood samples to determine if they were infected by one mosquito or six different mosquitoes.

Later on Wednesday, public health officials in Frankfurt sent a letter to media outlets which said two of the affected individuals had died.

"For the population of Frankfurt, the risk is considered very, very low. The disease is not transmissible from person to person but is always transmitted by mosquitoes," the letter added.

It said laboratory tests to determine the source of the infections were not expected to be available for several weeks.

The Robert Koch Institute - a German federal government agency and research institute for disease control and public health - previously said the four employees fell ill between 4 and 6 July and the mosquitoes were brought in by plane.

The institute said malaria in Germany almost exclusively affects long-haul travellers who were infected in malaria-endemic areas, and that malaria transmitted within a German airport is rare.

"The lack of a travel history can lead to a delayed diagnosis. A delayed diagnosis increases the risk of a severe course of the diseases," the institute said in its epidemiological bulletin.

The last case of airport malaria was in 2023 also at Frankfurt Airport, it added.

Malaria is a disease spread by some types of mosquitoes biting humans, and is mostly found in tropical countries, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The infection, which is preventable and curable, is caused by a parasite and does not spread from person to person. However symptoms can be mild or life-threatening.
body.zh: 法兰克福机场罕见爆发疟疾，导致六名员工感染由蚊子传播的严重感染，两名工作人员死于疟疾。 据德国公共卫生官员称，据信这些蚊子是乘飞机抵达德国最繁忙的机场，引发了疫情，并于 7 月份首次发现。 机场运营商法兰克福机场服务全球公司的发言人告诉英国广播公司，一名员工因感染而死亡，而公共卫生官员周三晚些时候表示，其中两名受影响的人已经死亡。 机场已安装捕蚊器，捕获的蚊子将在实验室进行分析，以确定其种类和来源。 法兰克福机场集团发言人告诉英国广播公司：“我们已向所有员工提供了全面的信息，并鼓励他们在出现任何症状时咨询医生。” 据英国广播公司了解，六名从事不同工作和机场不同区域的男性机场工作人员被感染，官员们正在分析血液样本，以确定他们是被一种蚊子感染还是被六种不同的蚊子感染。 周三晚些时候，法兰克福的公共卫生官员致函媒体，称其中两名受影响者已经死亡。 信中补充说：“对于法兰克福居民来说，这种风险被认为非常非常低。这种疾病不会在人与人之间传播，而是总是通过蚊子传播。” 报告称，预计数周内无法进行确定感染源的实验室检测。 德国联邦政府机构兼疾病控制和公共卫生研究所罗伯特·科赫研究所此前表示，这四名员工于7月4日至6日期间患病，蚊子是由飞机带来的。 该研究所表示，德国的疟疾几乎只影响在疟疾流行地区感染的长途旅行者，而在德国机场内传播的疟疾很少见。 该研究所在流行病学通报中表示：“缺乏旅行史可能会导致诊断延迟。延迟诊断会增加疾病严重发展的风险。” 报告补充说，最后一例机场疟疾也是 2023 年在法兰克福机场发生的。 据世界卫生组织（WHO）称，疟疾是一种由某些类型的蚊子叮咬人类传播的疾病，主要见于热带国家。 这种感染是可预防和治愈的，由寄生虫引起，不会在人与人之间传播。然而，症状可能很轻微或危及生命。

title.en: Trump officials threaten Kennedy Center demolition if court blocks renovations
title.zh: 特朗普官员威胁称，如果法院阻止翻修工程，将拆除肯尼迪中心

summary.en: The justice department has also asked for Trump's name to be put back on the building after it was removed in June following a court order.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Trump administration has threatened to demolish the Kennedy Center if planned renovations for the performing arts venue are not allowed to be carried out, court documents show.

Attorneys from the justice department have also asked for President Donald Trump's name to be put back on the building after it was removed in June following a court order.

"An order blocking the Board from appropriately recognising President Trump," the lawyers argued, "will cause donors to flee, financial contributions to dry up, and structural rehabilitation to stop".

The venue has been among the storied sites in Washington that Trump has sought to renovate since he returned to the White House in 2025.

Trump's lawyers have argued that without the renovations the venue "will deteriorate further into an unsafe, decrepit structure that will be required to be taken down".

After the "decrepit structure" is taken down, justice department attorney Brantley Mayers wrote, a determination of what to build on the site will follow, including the option of a large outdoor amphitheatre overlooking the Potomac River.

The threat to demolish the building comes just weeks after the Kennedy Center board voted to add Trump's name back to the facade of the venue and to proceed with a two-year closure for proposed renovations.

Many of the board members who voted are Trump allies who were appointed by the president.

In late May, a US judge ruled that the president's name had been added to the venue unlawfully, as it cannot be renamed without congressional approval.

The case stemmed from a broader legal dispute over the renaming of the cultural institution, which US law designates as a memorial to President John F Kennedy.

It is the latest in series of projects that Trump has taken on since returning to Washington.

He has been renovating the reflecting pool on the National Mall, he wants to construct a 250-foot victory arch , has demolished the White House East Wing to build a ballroom , and has added his name to institutions such as the Kennedy Center and US Institute of Peace.
body.zh: 法庭文件显示，特朗普政府威胁称，如果不批准对表演艺术场馆进行计划的翻修，将拆除肯尼迪中心。 司法部的律师还要求将唐纳德·特朗普总统的名字重新印在该建筑上，该建筑于 6 月根据法院命令被拆除。 律师们辩称，“阻止委员会适当承认特朗普总统的命令将导致捐助者逃离、财政捐助枯竭、结构修复停止”。 该场馆是特朗普自 2025 年重返白宫以来一直寻求翻新的华盛顿著名景点之一。 特朗普的律师辩称，如果不进行翻修，该场馆“将进一步恶化为不安全、破旧的结构，需要拆除”。 司法部律师布兰特利·梅耶斯写道，在“破旧的建筑”被拆除后，将决定在该地点建造什么，包括选择建造一个俯瞰波托马克河的大型户外圆形剧场。 就在几周前，肯尼迪中心董事会投票决定将特朗普的名字重新添加到场馆的正面，并继续关闭两年以进行拟议的翻修，就有人威胁拆除该建筑。 许多投票的董事会成员都是由总统任命的特朗普盟友。 5月下旬，一名美国法官裁定，总统的名字被非法添加到会场中，因为未经国会批准不得更名。 该案源于有关文化机构更名的更广泛的法律纠纷，美国法律将其指定为约翰·F·肯尼迪总统的纪念碑。 这是特朗普返回华盛顿以来实施的一系列项目中的最新一个。 他一直在翻新国家广场上的倒影池，他想要建造一座250英尺高的胜利拱门，拆除了白宫东翼以建造一个舞厅，并将他的名字写在肯尼迪中心和美国和平研究所等机构上。

title.en: Door was locked at Pakistan hospital where fire killed 14 babies, witnesses say
title.zh: 目击者称巴基斯坦医院门被锁，火灾导致14名婴儿死亡

summary.en: The hospital tells the BBC the ward door was not locked but manned with security guards, to protect the babies.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
It was just after dawn on Wednesday morning at a maternity ward in the Pakistani capital when a horrific blaze erupted.

It would go on to kill 14 infants as parents say they waited hours for help to arrive.

Hivsa Walid was near the room at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital with her sister-in-law, who had given birth days earlier. She initially heard a shout and thought a patient had died - but then she saw smoke.

"We didn't even think about our belongings. We just grabbed the baby and rushed downstairs.

"Some patients had delivered their babies just that night. I don't even know how we managed to get down - it was all a blur."

The fire broke out in an air-conditioning unit on the third floor of the mother and child unit at PIMS, one of the main state-run hospitals in Islamabad. Only one of the 15 babies present was saved.

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP news agency there was a long wait for rescue workers. "I lost my daughter. She was only three days old," he said.

Jaweria, the mother of another victim, told AFP news agency the door to the maternity ward was locked.

"For two hours I kept crying and wailing," she said. "Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate."

"To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them."

Rana Imran Sikander, the hospital's executive director, told the BBC the ward's door was not locked but was manned. He cited the need to protect babies from being stolen, something that has happened before at government hospitals.

Walid suggested PIMS's safety protocols were inadequate, despite it being a major hospital. "There should have been fire extinguishers and protocols, but no one was doing anything - everyone was just running."

The father of a baby who died told Reuters he had been visiting the ward for eight days and the building had "no fire security, no proper exits".

"All doors were closed, only one door was for us to visit our children. They kept the other doors locked because they feared we would come to see our children too often."

People had to "break the door down" and rescue teams were forced to smash the windows to control the flames, a witness who did not give her name told AFP.

Abdul Ghafoor, another witness, told AFP he tried to get into the building to rescue patients but couldn't reach the maternity ward.

"There was thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped," he said. "Rescue teams arrived after almost two hours."

Islamabad's Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf said rescue teams reached the scene "immediately" after the emergency call was first made, according to AFP.

PIMS is one of the biggest hospitals in Pakistan's capital, with 156 beds in its maternal and child health unit.

body.zh: 周三早上天刚亮，巴基斯坦首都的一个产科病房就爆发了可怕的大火。 这导致 14 名婴儿死亡，父母称他们等了好几个小时才得到救援。 希夫萨·瓦利德 (Hivsa Walid) 和几天前刚生完孩子的嫂子在巴基斯坦医学科学研究所 (PIMS) 医院的病房附近。她最初听到一声喊叫，以为一名病人已经死亡，但随后她看到了烟雾。 “我们根本没有考虑自己的财物，抱起婴儿就冲下楼。 “有些病人当天晚上就生下了孩子。我什至不知道我们是怎么下来的——一切都是一片模糊。” 火灾发生在伊斯兰堡主要公立医院之一 PIMS 母婴病房三楼的空调设备内。在场的 15 名婴儿中只有 1 人获救。 40 岁的库拉姆·马穆德 (Khurram Mehmood) 告诉法新社，救援人员等待了很长时间。 “我失去了我的女儿。她只有三天大，”他说。 另一名受害者的母亲贾韦里亚告诉法新社，产房的门是锁着的。 “两个小时以来我一直在哭泣，”她说。 “警察四小时后到达，并表示他们来这里调查。” “让你们见鬼去吧，救援队和警察。婴儿在那里被烧死，但没有人能救他们。” 医院执行主任拉纳·伊姆兰·西坎德 (Rana Imran Sikander) 告诉 BBC，病房的门没有锁，但有人看管。他提到需要保护婴儿不被偷走，这种情况以前在政府医院发生过。 瓦利德表示，尽管 PIMS 是一家大型医院，但它的安全规程并不充分。 “应该有灭火器和协议，但没有人做任何事情——每个人都在奔跑。” 一名死亡婴儿的父亲告诉路透社，他已经来病房八天了，该建筑“没有消防安全，没有适当的出口”。 “所有的门都关着，只有一扇门供我们探望孩子。他们把其他门都锁上了，因为他们担心我们会经常来看望我们的孩子。” 一位不愿透露姓名的目击者告诉法新社，人们不得不“破门而入”，救援队被迫砸碎窗户以控制火势。 另一位目击者阿卜杜勒·加福尔告诉法新社，他试图进入大楼营救病人，但无法到达产科病房。 “里面冒出浓浓的黑烟，病人被困，”他说。 “救援队在近两个小时后到达。” 据法新社报道，伊斯兰堡首席专员苏海尔·阿什拉夫表示，救援队在接到紧急电话后“立即”到达现场。 PIMS 是巴基斯坦首都最大的医院之一，其妇幼保健部门拥有 156 张床位。 国家...

title.en: Meta settles in US states lawsuit on teen user addiction
title.zh: Meta 在美国各州针对青少年用户成瘾的诉讼中达成和解

summary.en: Meta has agreed to pay what could amount to billions of dollars and to implement platform usage limitations on young users in a lawsuit brought by US states. The challenge revolved around addiction issues and overuse.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 在美国各州提起的诉讼中，Meta 同意支付可能高达数十亿美元的费用，并对年轻用户实施平台使用限制。挑战围绕成瘾问题和过度使用。 Facebook 和 Instagram 的母公司 Meta 同意支付高达 167 亿美元（约合 143 亿欧元），并对青少年使用其社交媒体网站的方式施加新的限制，作为美国多个州在加利福尼亚州提起诉讼的一部分。 该提案于周三向联邦法院提交，旨在解决美国总共 47 个州联盟提出的索赔要求。 除了经济损失之外，预计 Meta 还会引入各种限制和变更，旨在改善儿童安全，阻止或防止夜间或上课期间的过度使用和社交媒体活动。 加州总检察长罗布·邦塔 (Rob Bonta) 在宣布和解协议时在一份声明中表示：“Meta 已同意进行大规模变革，以降低其平台造成损害的风险，并将在几个月内完成。” 他称该协议是“真正的改变、真正的透明度以及对儿童的真正可执行的保护”。 该文件指出，该协议并不意味着 Meta 承认责任或不当行为，Meta 一直否认这些指控。 然而，弗吉尼亚州总检察长杰伊·琼斯认为，梅塔故意将年轻人的健康置于危险之中，而这些变化有助于阻止这种情况。 琼斯说：“多年来，Meta 故意欺骗公众，让公众了解其令人上瘾和有害的设计功能，这些功能对青少年的心理健康造成了严重破坏。”他认为，和解协议“将结束这些危险的做法，并提供有意义的救济，保护儿童免受网络伤害。” Meta 提出了针对 18 岁以下人群的一系列使用限制，其中包括对每天在其网站上花费的总时间设置“硬性上限”。 Meta 各个平台的全天累积上限设置为每日使用 2 小时。家长将有权解除限制。 Meta 表示，如果它检测到拥有多个帐户的不同用户，它将适用于所有用户。 午夜至早上 6 点期间，未成年用户也将被暂停使用该网站。 在 Meta 所称的“学校模式”中，通知将在上午 8 点到下午 3 点之间默认静音，青少年在这些时间段内不再收到推送通知，“除了有关其帐户安全的直接消息和警报”。 在美国大多数州，在 Facebook 和 Instagram 上开设帐户的最低年龄为 13 岁（在某些情况下甚至更高），因此理论上对于年幼的孩子来说应该没有问题。加州总检察长表示...

title.en: Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
title.zh: 叙利亚会成为以色列与土耳其冲突的焦点吗？

summary.en: An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.

Following US mediation, Syrian and Israeli representatives met in Jordan last weekend for the first time in months. The talks aimed to defuse tensions following the recent Israeli attacks on Syrian territory and prevent hostilities between Israel and Turkey from spilling over into Syria.

The escalation was sparked by an Israeli attack on the Abu Duhur military airfield in Idlib Province on August 18. According to Syrian sources, the attack struck the runway and storage facilities without causing any fatalities. Israel stated that Syria had violated — or threatened to violate — a previous security agreement by allowing Turkish troops to use the airfield. Damascus and Ankara rejected these allegations.

 The US criticized the attack by its Israeli ally as an "unnecessary escalation." In diplomatic terms, this amounts to a fairly clear show of rhetorical support for Ankara  and Damascus .

Israel views a potential Turkish military presence in Syria as a red line . Yet, it remains unclear whether such a deployment is planned in the long term or whether it was even imminent at the time of the attack. Evidence on this matter is not publicly available.

However, as early as April 2025, Reuters news agency cited anonymous sources saying Turkey had inspected at least three air bases in Syria  where it might want to station troops  as part of a planned joint defense pact. Israeli airstrikes were already taking place at that time as well.

The Washington-based think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), which is considered pro-Israel, justifies the attack as follows : "Israel worries that Ankara could eventually use its military presence in Syria as a platform to pressure or threaten Israel, and remains wary of the close relationship between Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa and the Turkish leadership."

For Bente Scheller, Syria expert at the German Green Party-affiliated Heinrich Böll Foundation, this explanation falls short.

"There is no evidence so far that Turkish troops are actually supposed to be stationed there," she told DW.  While Israel may indeed have its own intelligence, the recent attack must be viewed against the backdrop of Israel's overall policy toward Syria as well as Turkey's growing regional role, she noted.

Marcus Schneider, a Middle East analyst at Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation — which is affiliated with the German Social Democratic Party (SPD) — in Beirut, also points out that a struggle for power and influence is unfolding in Syria and beyond.

body.zh: 不久前以色列对叙利亚军用机场的袭击再次表明，叙利亚正在成为地区大国博弈的关键战场。走在前列的是以色列和土耳其。 在美国的调解下，叙利亚和以色列代表上周末在约旦举行了数月来的首次会面。会谈旨在缓和以色列最近袭击叙利亚领土后的紧张局势，并防止以色列和土耳其之间的敌对行动蔓延到叙利亚。 事态升级是由以色列8月18日袭击伊德利卜省阿布杜胡尔军用机场引发的。叙利亚消息人士称，这次袭击袭击了跑道和储存设施，没有造成任何人员死亡。以色列表示，叙利亚允许土耳其军队使用该机场，违反了或威胁违反了之前的安全协议。大马士革和安卡拉否认了这些指控。 美国批评其盟友以色列的袭击是“不必要的升级”。从外交角度来说，这相当于对安卡拉和大马士革相当明确的口头支持。 以色列将土耳其在叙利亚的潜在军事存在视为红线。然而，目前尚不清楚这种部署是否是长期计划，或者在袭击发生时是否迫在眉睫。有关此事的证据尚未公开。 然而，早在 2025 年 4 月，路透社就援引匿名消息人士的话说，土耳其已经检查了叙利亚的至少三个空军基地，作为计划中的联合防御协议的一部分，土耳其可能希望在那里驻军。以色列当时也已经开始空袭。 总部位于华盛顿的智库捍卫民主基金会（FDD）被认为是亲以色列的，它为这次袭击辩护如下：“以色列担心安卡拉最终可能利用其在叙利亚的军事存在作为向以色列施压或威胁的平台，并对叙利亚总统艾哈迈德·沙拉和土耳其领导人之间的密切关系保持警惕。” 对于德国绿党下属的海因里希伯尔基金会的叙利亚专家本特·谢勒来说，这种解释是不够的。 她告诉德国之声：“到目前为止，没有证据表明土耳其军队实际上应该驻扎在那里。” 她指出，虽然以色列可能确实拥有自己的情报，但必须在以色列对叙利亚的总体政策以及土耳其日益增强的地区作用的背景下看待最近的袭击。 德国弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会（隶属于德国社会民主党（SPD））驻贝鲁特的中东分析师马库斯·施奈德也指出，叙利亚及其他地区正在展开权力和影响力的斗争。 “这次袭击主要引发了......

title.en: Zambia after the polls: A test for democracy in Africa
title.zh: 赞比亚大选后：对非洲民主的考验

summary.en: Zambia's democratic institutions are under scrutiny, as the opposition continues to dispute the election results and courts remain closed. Weeks after the election, Zambia’s election story might be far from over.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Zambia's democratic institutions are under scrutiny, as the opposition continues to dispute the election results and courts remain closed. Weeks after the election, Zambia’s election story might be far from over.

The Electoral Commission of Zambia has declared incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema winner of the August 13 presidential election .

His closest challenger, Brian Mundubile, received 38% of the vote, according to official results published last week. However, Mundubile has since announced on several occasions that he would be challenging that result , and that his National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) "shall not relent" in the face of any obstacle.

That challenge, however, comes as Zambia's courts have all remained closed since August 24 until further notice, with officials citing "security concerns."

The timing of this closure has raised questions about opposition voices having access to judicial election safeguards during this crucial stage of the post-election process, as random reports of irregularities continue to surface.

The Law Association of Zambia (LAZ) has called for the urgent restoration of access to the courts and for alternative arrangements to be enacted for urgent cases.

LAZ President Arnold Kaluba said security measures must not undermine any access to justice or judicial independence.

"Such measures must be lawful, proportionate and implemented in a manner that preserves access to justice and respects the constitutional independence and autonomy of the judiciary," he stressed.

Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Zambia has also expressed concern; its chairperson, Pamela Towela Sambo, warned that disruption to judicial operations could affect fundamental rights in the country, including access to a fair trial and legal remedies.

"[If] the right to a fair trial is delayed, there is increased risk of arbitrary detentions, while access to remedies is effectively blocked," she said.

However, the ongoing election dispute has taken a new turn: Zambia's Chief Justice Mumba Malila, acknowledged on August 25 that he had received documents described as a presidential election petition through his private email-address.

Malila described the method of submission as "highly irregular" —despite the current circumstances allowing no access to legal procedures. He said he nevertheless referred the documents to the Constitutional Court to determine whether this qualified as a petition having been formally filed.

The distinction here is important: The receipt of such documents does not confirm that a presidential election petition has been formally lodged per se.

body.zh: 赞比亚的民主机构正受到审查，反对派继续对选举结果提出异议，法院仍然关闭。选举几周后，赞比亚的选举故事可能还远没有结束。 赞比亚选举委员会宣布现任总统哈坎德·希奇莱马 (Hakainde Hichilema) 在 8 月 13 日的总统选举中获胜。 根据上周公布的官方结果，他最接近的挑战者布莱恩·蒙杜比莱 (Brian Mundubile) 获得了 38% 的选票。然而，蒙杜比莱此后多次宣布他将挑战这一结果，并且他的民族团结与繁荣和解党（NRPUP）面对任何障碍“都不会松懈”。 然而，这一挑战正值赞比亚所有法院自 8 月 24 日以来一直关闭，直至另行通知，官员们以“安全问题”为由。 随着关于违规行为的随机报告不断浮出水面，关闭的时机引发了人们对反对派声音在选举后进程的关键阶段能否获得司法选举保障的质疑。 赞比亚法律协会 (LAZ) 呼吁紧急恢复诉诸法庭的机会，并针对紧急案件制定替代安排。 LAZ 主席阿诺德·卡鲁巴 (Arnold Kaluba) 表示，安全措施不得损害任何诉诸司法的机会或司法独立。 他强调说：“此类措施必须合法、相称，并以维护诉诸司法的机会并尊重宪法规定的司法独立和自治的方式实施。” 与此同时，赞比亚人权委员会也表达了担忧；其主席帕梅拉·托维拉·桑博 (Pamela Towela Sambo) 警告称，司法运作中断可能会影响该国的基本权利，包括获得公平审判和法律补救的机会。 “[如果]公平审判的权利被推迟，任意拘留的风险就会增加，而获得补救的机会实际上就会受到阻碍，”她说。 然而，正在进行的选举争议出现了新的转折：赞比亚首席大法官蒙巴·马利拉 (Mumba Malila) 于 8 月 25 日承认，他通过其私人电子邮件地址收到了所谓总统选举请愿书的文件。 马里拉将提交方式描述为“高度不规范”——尽管目前情况不允许诉诸法律程序。他说，尽管如此，他还是将这些文件提交给宪法法院，以确定这是否符合正式提交请愿书的资格。 这里的区别很重要：收到此类文件并不确认总统选举请愿书本身已正式提交。 最新进展是在法院仍然...

title.en: India: Assam tea industry faces climate-driven labor crisis
title.zh: 印度：阿萨姆邦茶叶产业面临气候驱动的劳工危机

summary.en: Plantations in Assam produce more than half of India's tea. But rising heat is hurting yields, workers are increasingly leaving for more stable work, and producers are feeling the squeeze of stagnant tea prices.
summary.zh: 阿萨姆邦的种植园生产了印度一半以上的茶叶。但气温升高正在损害产量，工人越来越多地离开去寻找更稳定的工作，而生产商则感受到茶叶价格停滞不前的压力。

body.en:
Plantations in Assam produce more than half of India's tea. But rising heat is hurting yields, workers are increasingly leaving for more stable work, and producers are feeling the squeeze of stagnant tea prices.

The problems facing upper Assam's tea gardens are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore for workers like Bidesh Kamar and Sumitra Tanti.

Recent floods disrupted work for weeks in the northeast Indian state , adding even more uncertainty to their already precarious livelihood. More than 50 tea gardens were damaged following a devastating storm that swept across parts of Assam.

"Life has become unpredictable," Tanti told DW. "The weather can disrupt work, while wages remain low and work is not as dependable as it once was," she added.

"Tea is not as profitable as it once was, and there is less certainty about the work," Kamar told DW.

After 15 years working on tea plantations, Kamar is now considering whether it is time to "move on to greener pastures."

Their experience points to a growing problem for Assam's tea industry. With the business becoming less profitable and working conditions more uncertain, the industry is struggling to retain the experienced workforce which forms the backbone of the state's tea production.

Assam produces about 52% of India's tea and supports around 700,000 plantation workers and 140,000 small tea growers.

For generations, its tea plantations have depended on a vast workforce picking leaves by hand.

But that model is now under pressure as the climate gets hotter , tea becomes less profitable and locals increasingly look elsewhere for work.

Oversupply has pushed prices down, while higher wages, fertilizer and fuel costs are squeezing producers.

Sanjiv Gogoi, who owns the 400-acre (162-hectare) Sanjiv Tea estate, said tea producers are grappling with a whole range of problems.

"Productivity has fallen, and the labor supply is not always reliable. More workers are leaving the plantations because the work no longer pays enough," Gogoi told DW.

The pressure is even greater on small growers, who produce nearly half of Assam's tea, he said.

"They have little bargaining power and often have to sell their freshly picked leaves to factories at low prices."

At the same time, erratic rainfall , rising temperatures and new pests are reducing yields and making traditional tea-growing areas increasingly vulnerable.

In Assam's major tea-growing districts, temperatures now regularly reach 36 to 40 degrees Celsius (97-104 degrees Fahrenheit), putting both tea plants and workers under severe heat stress .

Research shows that every 1°C rise in temperature can reduce tea yields by about 87 kilos per hectare in India.

body.zh: 印度一半以上的茶叶产自阿萨姆邦的种植园。但气温上升正在损害产量，越来越多的工人离开去寻找更稳定的工作，生产商也感受到了茶叶价格停滞的压力。 对于像比德什·卡马尔（Bidesh Kamar）和苏米特拉·坦蒂（Sumitra Tanti）这样的工人来说，阿萨姆邦上游茶园面临的问题变得越来越难以忽视。 最近的洪水使印度东北部邦的工作中断了数周，给他们本已岌岌可危的生计增添了更多的不确定性。一场席卷阿萨姆邦部分地区的毁灭性风暴导致 50 多个茶园遭到破坏。 “生活变得不可预测，”坦蒂告诉德国之声。 “天气可能会扰乱工作，而工资仍然很低，工作也不像以前那么可靠，”她补充道。 卡马尔告诉德国之声：“茶叶不再像以前那样有利可图，而且工作的确定性也降低了。” 在茶园工作了 15 年之后，卡马尔现在正在考虑是否是时候“转向更绿色的牧场”了。 他们的经验表明阿萨姆邦茶业面临着一个日益严重的问题。随着业务利润下降和工作条件更加不确定，该行业正在努力留住经验丰富的劳动力，而这些劳动力构成了该州茶叶生产的支柱。 阿萨姆邦生产印度约 52% 的茶叶，养活着约 70 万名种植园工人和 14 万名小型茶农。 几代人以来，茶园一直依赖大量劳动力手工采摘茶叶。 但随着气候变暖、茶叶利润下降以及当地人越来越多地到其他地方寻找工作，这种模式现在面临压力。 供应过剩导致价格下跌，而工资、化肥和燃料成本的上涨则给生产商带来压力。 Sanjiv Gogoi 拥有占地 400 英亩（162 公顷）的 Sanjiv 茶园，他表示茶叶生产商正在努力解决一系列问题。 “生产力下降，劳动力供应并不总是可靠。越来越多的工人离开种植园，因为工作报酬不再足够，”戈戈伊告诉德国之声。 他说，小种植者面临的压力更大，他们生产阿萨姆邦近一半的茶叶。 “他们几乎没有议价能力，常常不得不以低价将刚采摘的叶子卖给工厂。” 与此同时，不稳定的降雨量、不断上升的气温和新出现的害虫正在降低产量，使传统茶产区变得越来越脆弱。 在阿萨姆邦的主要茶产区，气温现在经常达到 36 至 40 摄氏度（97-104 华氏度），使茶树和工人都承受着严重的热应激。 研究表明，气温每升高 1°C，印度每公顷茶叶产量就会减少约 87 公斤。 对于花几个小时在户外采摘茶叶的茶叶工人来说，...

title.en: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally Eswatini over 'security risks'
title.zh: 中国建议其公民因“安全风险”离开台湾盟友斯威士兰

summary.en: Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China's foreign ministry has told its citizens to leave the southern African kingdom of Eswatini over "security risks".

The ministry cited "rampant cyber fraud and criminal activities associated with gambling" as among its security concerns, but did not give details.

It suggested its citizens relocate as soon as possible to "relatively safer" countries such as neighbouring South Africa.

Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which China claims as part of its territory.

On Tuesday, the privately owned Times of Eswatini news site reported that 40 Chinese nationals have been in detention since last month , external after being arrested while trying to leave the country.

They were first arrested - along with dozens of other foreign nationals - in March during raids on alleged illegal online gambling centres in the main city, Mbabane, and surrounding areas, the news site reported.

The group's lawyers had written to the attorney general and home affairs ministry, stating that they had pleaded guilty to immigration-related offences and had paid fines imposed by the courts, the news site reported.

The 40 were then released on the orders of the High Court, and their re-arrest was unlawful, the lawyers were quoted as saying.

In its advisory to its citizens, China says those who insist on travelling to or staying in the country will face "extremely high security risks, and the timeliness of assistance may be affected".

China has for years pressured countries to end diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

In April, Taiwan accused Beijing of trying to derail its President Lai Ching-te's travel to Eswatini by pressuring nearby countries to revoke overflight permits.

The trip, originally planned for 22-26 April to mark the 40th anniversary of Eswatini's King Mswati III's accession, was cancelled following the development.

Lai eventually travelled to Eswatini in May, without saying how he reached the country. None of the governments had announced the trip beforehand.

Following the visit, Beijing's foreign ministry said that Lai had become "an international laughing stock".

Earlier this year, China scrapped tariffs for all African countries, except Eswatini.
body.zh: 由于“安全风险”，中国外交部已要求其公民离开南部非洲斯威士兰王国。 该部将“猖獗的网络欺诈和与赌博相关的犯罪活动”列为其安全担忧之一，但没有提供细节。 它建议其公民尽快搬迁到邻国南非等“相对安全”的国家。 斯威士兰是 12 个国家之一，也是非洲唯一一个与台湾建交的国家，中国声称台湾是其领土的一部分。 周二，私营新闻网站《斯威士兰时报》报道称，自上个月以来，已有 40 名中国公民在试图离开该国时被捕，并在境外被拘留。 据新闻网站报道，他们与其他数十名外国人一起于 3 月份在对主要城市姆巴巴内及周边地区涉嫌非法在线赌博中心的突袭中首次被捕。 据新闻网站报道，该组织的律师已写信给总检察长和内政部，表示他们已承认与移民有关的罪行，并已支付法院判处的罚款。 律师称，这 40 人随后根据高等法院的命令被释放，再次逮捕他们是非法的。 中国在向公民发出的建议中表示，那些坚持前往或留在中国的人将面临“极高的安全风险，援助的及时性可能受到影响”。 多年来，中国一直向各国施压，要求它们终止与台湾的外交关系。 今年四月，台湾指责北京试图向周边国家施压，要求吊销飞越许可，从而破坏台湾总统赖清德前往斯威士兰的行程。 这次旅行原计划于4月22日至26日举行，以纪念斯威士兰国王姆斯瓦蒂三世登基40周年，但因事态发展而被取消。 赖最终于五月前往斯威士兰，但没有透露他是如何到达该国的。没有任何一个政府事先宣布这次访问。 访问结束后，北京外交部表示赖已成为“国际笑柄”。 今年早些时候，中国取消了对除斯威士兰以外的所有非洲国家的关税。

title.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏突发致命洪灾，多个村庄被冲毁

summary.en: Dozens of people have died and hundreds are missing after flash floods swept through remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet. Rescue efforts have been hampered by high water levels, preventing helicopters from landing, while authorities work to relocate families from high-risk areas. At least 157 bodies have been recovered...
summary.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏的偏远山谷遭遇突发洪灾，造成数十人死亡，数百人失踪。由于水位过高，救援直升机无法降落，救援工作严重受阻。目前当局正努力将高风险地区的家庭转移，警方已找回157具遗体，失踪人员中还包括341名外国游客。

body.en:
Dozens have died and hundreds were reported missing, including 341 foreign tourists. Rescue helicopters have been unable to land in affected areas due to high floodwaters.

Dozens of people were confirmed dead and hundreds more are missing after a flash flood swept through remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday.

Nepali police said that authorities have recovered 157 bodies. Officers were "working to move families in flood-risk areas... to safer locations," police said.

"The pain and loss you have suffered is not small. But I want to assure you that you are not alone in this difficult time -- the state is with you with all its means and resources," Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a statement posted to social media. "Please be patient. The government takes full responsibility for your rescue, treatment, food and shelter. In times of such a disaster, we all need to stand together."

In China, authorities said at least three have died, with 265 still missing, China's state broadcaster CCTV ‌said.

The floodwaters washed away villages, damaged bridges and destroyed electrical infrastructure on both sides of the Nepal-China border.

"There is devastation everywhere we look," ‌Tula ​Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa district, told Reuters.

"The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing."

At the same time, Chinese authorities also reported that a mudslide caused "major casualties" on the other side of the border in Tibet.

Nepal's Tourism Ministry said 403 travelers were reported missing for several hours after the floods struck. 

Missing travelers included 341 foreign tourists, among them 142  Indians . Other nationalities of those missing included people from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea and the United States, the tourism board said.

A Nepali police spokesperson told Germany's DPA news agency that dozens of personnel were also missing.

"So far, we only have confirmation of 26 police personnel who remain missing in the flood," they said.

"We also have missing information of government revenue officials, hydropower workers among others. But we are still collecting the data."

Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said an earthquake triggered an avalanche in the Himalayas that then triggered flash floods in the valleys below.

Chinese state news agency Xinhua said a mudslide on the Nepali side of the mountains spread to Gyirong County in Tibet.

"Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out," said David Fisher, the Nepal head of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).

reflection.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏偏远村庄遭遇的突发毁灭，提醒着我们人类生命与自然原始力量之间脆弱的边界。当救援直升机在不断上涨的水位中艰难寻找降落点时，我们看到这个世界尚未达到它应有的样子，充满了美丽却也伴随着突如其来的危险。在这些“叹息”的时刻，我们寻求雅伟的同在，求祂扶持哀恸的人，并指引救援者的双手。

title.en: Around the world, people are rejecting divisive and dangerous politics. We can – and must – build on that | Gordon Brown
title.zh: 在世界各地，人们正在拒绝分裂和危险的政治。我们可以而且必须在此基础上再接再厉|戈登·布朗

summary.en: The vast majority of the global public wants international cooperation on human rights, climate and AI. Like-minded countries must stand together to deliver Britain’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, is already having to make one of his gravest decisions. He has to issue the...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: The vast majority of the global public wants international cooperation on human rights, climate and AI. Like-minded countries must stand together to deliver Britain’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, is already having to make one of his gravest decisions. He has to issue the instructions that he alone gives to the military, setting out the UK response in a doomsday scenario of a nuclear weapons attack on us. He will, as I did two decades ago, sign a piece of paper telling commanders whether or not to retaliate and, if so, whether through targeting civilian conurbations or military sites. These instructions are written down in the aptly named “letter of last resort” . Now, more than at any time since the 1960s Cuban missile crisis, the European public fears a third world war . With the nuclear Doomsday Clock developed by atomic scientists moving ever closer to midnight, and Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, Poland and Germany contemplating either acquiring nuclear weapons or siting them on their soil , our world is descending from a rules-based order to a power-based one, where might is deemed right and brute force dominates. Gordon Brown is the UN’s special envoy for global education and was UK prime minister from 2007 to 2010 The future starts with us: Gordon Brown in conversation On Thursday 10 September, join Hugh Muir and Gordon Brown to discuss the intricate connections between global instability and civic decline, as explored in Brown’s new book, The Future Starts With Us . Book tickets here Continue reading...
body.zh: 全球绝大多数公众希望在人权、气候和人工智能方面开展国际合作。志同道合的国家必须团结起来，让英国新首相安迪·伯纳姆(Andy Burnham) 不得不做出他最重大的决定之一。他必须向军方发出他独自发出的指示，规定英国在核武器袭击我们的世界末日情景中的反应。他将像二十年前我所做的那样，签署一份文件，告诉指挥官是否进行报复，如果是，是否通过针对民用城市或军事地点进行报复。这些指示写在恰如其分的“最后手段信”中。现在，欧洲公众比 20 世纪 60 年代古巴导弹危机以来的任何时候都更加担心第三次世界大战。随着原子科学家研制出的核末日时钟越来越接近午夜，日本、韩国、沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋、埃及、波兰和德国正在考虑要么获得核武器，要么将它们部署在自己的土地上，我们的世界正在从基于规则的秩序下降到基于权力的秩序，在这个秩序中，强权被认为是正确的，暴力占主导地位。戈登·布朗 (Gordon Brown) 是联合国全球教育特使，曾于 2007 年至 2010 年担任英国首相 未来从我们开始：戈登·布朗对话 9 月 10 日星期四，与休·缪尔 (Hugh Muir) 和戈登·布朗 (Gordon Brown) 一起讨论全球不稳定与公民衰退之间的错综复杂的联系，正如布朗的新书《未来从我们开始》中所探讨的那样。在这里订票继续阅读...

title.en: China: Dissident artist jailed for satirical Mao sculptures
title.zh: 中国：持不同政见艺术家因讽刺毛泽东雕塑而入狱

summary.en: Sculptor Gao Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs." His supporters have called for his immediate release.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Sculptor Gao Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs." His supporters have called for his immediate release.

A court in China has reportedly sentenced a dissident artist to three years in jail for sculptures which satirized former Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong .

Sculptor Gao Zhen, 70, became famous in the 2000s for addressing sensitive topics in China such as the 1966-1976 Cultural Revolution or the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre through artworks he produced with his younger brother Gao Qiang.

Zhen, who is based in New York , was arrested during a visit to Beijing in August 2024. He was tried this year ⁠in a ⁠one-day behind-closed-doors trial and found guilty of "infringing upon the reputation of heroes."

"We feel outraged," Gao's wife Zhao Yaliang told the Reuters news agency. "Ever since I learned of the ​verdict, I haven't been able to recover from it. It's devastating."

Zhao also said she and her son, who is a US citizen, had been barred from leaving China since Zhen's detention two years ago.

Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs," legislation which came into effect in 2018 and was strengthened in ​2021.

The artworks found to have broken the law, however, date to 2005 and 2009, according to Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders who has been advocating for Gao's case.

"The court has now sentenced him to three years ... for artwork he made as far back as 2005, some 16 years before the law he was charged under even existed," Yi told Reuters, calling the punishment "a very clear case of a violation of a person's freedom of expression."

The artworks in question are reported to be "Mao's Guilt," a 2009 bronze statue of the former leader kneeling remorsefully, and the "Miss Mao" series of caricatures which depict Mao with breasts and a Pinocchio-like nose.

"No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history," Amnesty's China Director Sarah Brooks told the Associated Press.

"The lengthy pre-trial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offense illustrate the authorities' determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression."

Researcher Yi said: "The only outcome that respects Gao Zhen's rights is his immediate, unconditional release."

If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as your Preferred Source on Google , so you'll always see our verified news first.
body.zh: 雕塑家高震被指控违反中国《英雄烈士保护法》。他的支持者呼吁立即释放他。 据报道，中国一家法院因讽刺前中国革命领袖毛泽东的雕塑而判处一名异见艺术家三年监禁。 70 岁的雕塑家高震在 2000 年代因与弟弟高强创作的作品探讨中国的敏感话题而闻名，例如 1966-1976 年的文化大革命或 1989 年的天安门广场大屠杀。 甄现居住在纽约，于 2024 年 8 月访问北京期间被捕。今年，他在为期一天的闭门审判中接受审判，并被判犯有“侵犯英雄声誉”罪。 “我们感到愤怒，”高的妻子赵亚良告诉路透社。 “自从我得知判决后，我一直无法从中恢复过来。这是毁灭性的。” 赵还表示，自从两年前甄被拘留以来，她和她的美国公民儿子就被禁止离开中国。 甄根据中国《英雄烈士保护法》受到指控，该法于 2018 年生效，并于 2021 年加强。 然而，据一直为高案辩护的中国人权卫士研究员谢恩·易 (Shane Yi) 表示，被发现违法的艺术品可追溯到 2005 年和 2009 年。 易告诉路透社，“法院现在判处他三年有期徒刑……因为他早在 2005 年就创作了艺术品，比他被指控的法律还早大约 16 年。”他称这一处罚是“一个非常明显的侵犯个人言论自由的案件”。 据报道，这些艺术品是2009年创作的前领导人悔恨跪下的铜像“毛泽东的罪孽”，以及描绘毛泽东胸部和匹诺曹鼻子的“毛小姐”系列漫画。 国际特赦组织中国部主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 告诉美联社：“任何艺术家都不应因创作挑战官方叙述或鼓励对历史进行批判性反思的作品而面临刑事处罚。” “长时间的审前拘留，以及最终决定对高震定罪并判处他最高三年徒刑，表明当局决心阻止其他人从事独立的艺术表达。” 易研究员说：“尊重高震权利的唯一结果就是立即无条件释放他。” 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国在关键矿产方面的竞争日益激烈，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能会在没有政策保护的情况下在几个月内开始。 洛伊研究所的分析发现，采矿最早可能在 2027 年开始，太平洋海底蕴藏着大量珍贵资源。 全球最大的两个经济体之间的竞争是由电池、武器系统和电网产生的需求驱动的。 研究表明，该地区各国在经济收益的承诺和生态系统、渔业、粮食安全、生计和文化遭受不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。 它认为，商业深海采矿国际治理框架的缺乏导致太平洋国家在没有国际商定保护的情况下进行谈判。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这也使得它们依赖于寻求海底采矿的公司起草的单独协议。 洛伊研究所的康纳·格雷厄姆写道：“对于陷入这场争夺关键矿产霸权的大国战争的太平洋岛国来说，这个经济提议很难拒绝。” “问题不在于太平洋国家不同意，而在于它们被迫与拥有更多资源、信息和法律能力的各方进行单独谈判，而旨在保护它们的国际框架已经陷入停滞。” 格雷厄姆表示，虽然澳大利亚尚未对太平洋深海采矿采取明确立场，但它拥有产生影响的地位、关系和机构存在。 这包括它是太平洋岛屿论坛的成员以及美国的长期盟友。 他说：“对尚未作为即将开始的活动条件的标准的承诺与其说是一项政策，不如说是一种弃权。” 包括澳大利亚在内的国家已开始签订关键矿物交易，这对许多新兴技术至关重要。 联邦政府宣布设立 12 亿美元的关键矿产战略储备，以确保对澳大利亚经济和国家安全至关重要的关键矿产的供应。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The prospect of deep-sea mining in the Pacific presents a stark choice for island nations, balancing potential economic gains against the risk of irreversible ecological damage. As the report warns of mining commencing without adequate policy guardrails, the words of 1 Corinthians 10:23 remind us that while many actions may be permissible, not all are truly...
reflection.zh: 太平洋深海采矿的前景给岛屿国家带来了严峻的选择，需要在潜在的经济收益与不可逆转的生态破坏风险之间取得平衡。正如报告警告，在缺乏充分政策保障的情况下，采矿可能即将开始，哥林多前书10:23提醒我们，虽然许多事情是合法的，但并非所有事情都有益处或能造就人。这种情况呼唤智慧，以辨别什么能真正造就社区并保护雅伟的创造，而不是仅仅追求权宜之计。

verse.textEn: "I have the right to do anything," you say — but not everything is beneficial. "I have the right to do anything" — but not everything is constructive.
verse.textZh: 凡事都可行，但不都有益处；凡事都可行，但不都造就人。

title.en: Sam was jailed for helping Hong Kong's protesters. He came home to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

"That time was the first time that I was really involved in a social event," said Lau, who’s now 30 and lives in exile in London.

Following large demonstrations, the CCP abandoned its plans...
body.zh: 8 月 25 日晚上 9 点半（澳大利亚东部标准时间）在 SBS 或 SBS On Demand 观看《Dateline》的最新一集《香港：一座沉默的城市》。 21岁的陈志森正准备离开香港到海外继续深造。 他曾参与一个学生活动团体，该团体收集糖果和洗漱用品，寄给香港 2019 年反政府抗议活动后入狱的人。 当局指责该组织利用这些物资在囚犯中赢得支持并煽动反对政府。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 2021年9月，Sam根据一年前通过的香港国家安全法被捕，并被判“颠覆国家政权罪”。 “监狱太糟糕了。我和大约二十个人同住一间牢房。最拥挤的时候，我们可能有四十个人，”他说。 他声称一些监狱官员故意虐待与抗议运动有关的囚犯。 “我不知道他们是出于个人信念还是奉命行事。但他们确实让我们的生活变得困难。” 出狱两年后，萨姆正在努力重建正常的生活。 他曾梦想成为一名教师或护士，但他的犯罪记录阻止了他从事这两种职业。 “自从出狱后，我感觉自己好像进入了一个更大的牢房，”他说。 相反，他正在接受培训，成为一名纪录片制片人，他说，决心捕捉香港的转变。 “无论香港的结果如何，无论未来是好还是坏，我都想留在这里，见证未来的变化。” 萨姆的故事就像许多其他香港年轻人一样，他们的生活因中国对香港自由的镇压而被打乱。这座城市曾经以其直言不讳的新闻界、独立的司法机构和政治反对派而闻名。 1997年，在英国统治150多年之后，香港在“一国两制”安排下回归中国，并承诺香港将保持高度自治。 和 Sam 一样，刘嘉敏也是中国回归后长大的一代人：既不是英国人，也不是真正的中国人。 青少年时期，卡门在中学领导了一场学生运动，反对中国共产党试图在香港学校引入“爱国主义”课程。 许多香港人担心这会在他们的城市宣扬中共版本的爱国主义。 “那次是我第一次真正参与社交活动，”现年 30 岁、流亡伦敦的刘说。 大规模示威后，中共放弃了计划……

reflection.en: The story of Sam returning to a silenced city after imprisonment highlights the profound impact of oppressive rule on a community. Yahweh's word reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion, bringing fear and helplessness to the people. In such times, we are called to remember the dignity of every individual and pray for justice and peace.
reflection.zh: 山姆在被囚禁后回到一个寂静的城市，这个故事凸显了压迫性统治对一个社区的深远影响。雅伟的话语提醒我们，邪恶的统治者如同咆哮的狮子，给人民带来恐惧和无助。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召要记住每个人的尊严，并为公义与和平祷告。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

title.en: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record
title.zh: 见证时刻：人形机器人打破博尔特百米纪录

summary.en: A humanoid robot developed in Beijing has completed a 100m sprint in 9.39 seconds, surpassing Usain Bolt's world record of 9.58 seconds. The event, held at the World Humanoid Robot Games, showcased advancements in robotics including boxing, football, and household tasks. While the robot's speed is a mechanical...
summary.zh: 在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，一台人形机器人以9.39秒的成绩完成了百米冲刺，超越了尤塞恩·博尔特9.58秒的世界纪录。此次活动展示了机器人在拳击、足球和家务处理等领域的进步。虽然机器人的速度是一个机械里程碑，但它也凸显了在模仿人类体能方面飞速的技术进步。

body.en:
A robot has outperformed humans by running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

The humanoid robot, developed by the Beijing Innovation Centre of Humanoid Robotics, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the event.

Eight-time Olympic gold medallist Bolt set the world record for humans in 2009, running 100m in 9.58 seconds.

The robot beat two others including one made by Chinese smartphone maker Honor - which the manufacturer says ran the distance in 9.32 seconds in a test run.

Other events at the robot games, which started on Saturday, include boxing and football, but also household tasks such as folding laundry.
body.zh: 在中国举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，机器人跑得比尤塞恩·博尔特 (Usain Bolt) 保持的 1 亿米短跑世界纪录还要快，从而超越了人类。 由北京仿人机器人创新中心研发的仿人机器人在比赛中跑出了9.39秒的成绩。 八届奥运会金牌得主博尔特在 2009 年以 9.58 秒跑完 100m 的成绩创造了人类世界纪录。 该机器人击败了另外两个机器人，其中包括中国智能手机制造商荣耀制造的一个机器人，该制造商表示，该机器人在测试运行中仅用了 9.32 秒就跑完了距离。 周六开始的机器人比赛的其他项目包括拳击和足球，还有叠衣服等家务活。

reflection.en: The sight of a machine clocking 9.39 seconds in Beijing challenges our understanding of physical limits and the 'prize' of athletic achievement. While a robot can be engineered for singular mechanical efficiency, the human race involves a holistic discipline of the soul and body that reflects the wisdom of Yahweh. We celebrate human ingenuity in creating...
reflection.zh: 在北京看到机器跑出9.39秒的成绩，挑战了我们对体能极限和竞技“奖赏”的理解。虽然机器人可以为了单一的机械效率而设计，但人类的赛程包含了反映雅伟智慧的身心全面操练。我们赞叹人类创造此类工具的智慧，但我们也记得，人的终极价值不在于成为最快的“机器”。

verse.textEn: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to get the prize.
verse.textZh: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人？你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。
